chief_complaint: Routine follow-up for management of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 72‑year‑old male with longstanding essential hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, hypertriglyceridemia and metabolic syndrome. He is on a three‑drug antihypertensive regimen (lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, amlodipine) and low‑dose extended‑release metformin. Recent laboratory data show a normal hemoglobin A1c (5.6%) but no recent blood pressure, lipid panel, or renal function values are available. He has had multiple wellness visits (12) and outpatient encounters (3) with no emergency or inpatient admissions, suggesting relative clinical stability. Socially, he reports limited social contact, social isolation, and unsatisfactory housing, which may affect adherence and overall health. Anemia has been present for decades, and chronic sinusitis is noted. No acute complaints are documented.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include acute bronchitis (2021), viral sinusitis (2018), intimate partner abuse (2021), multiple episodes of stress (2019, 2021), and prior part‑time employment. These reflect past acute infections and psychosocial stressors that have since resolved.
